A1.title: Elif and Tom
A1.text: Hello! I am Elif. I am twelve. I am a student in Izmir. This is my friend Tom. He is from England. He is eleven. Tom is very nice and he is funny. We are in the same class. Our teacher is Ms Kaya. She is kind. Today Tom is tired, but I am happy. Goodbye, Tom! See you tomorrow!
q: How is Elif today? (Elif bugün nasıl?)
Who is Ms Kaya? (Ms Kaya kim?)

A1.title: My Family
A1.text: I have got a big family. My mother is a doctor. Her name is Leyla. My father is a teacher. His name is Ahmet. I have got one brother and two sisters. My brother's name is Can. He has got a black cat. Its name is Pamuk. My grandmother and grandfather are with us. My cousin Mert is from Ankara. He has got a red bike.
q: What is the writer's father? (Yazarın babası ne iş yapar?)
What has Can got? (Can'ın neyi var?)
Where is cousin Mert from? (Kuzen Mert nereli?)

A1.title: In the Classroom
A1.text: This is our classroom. It is on the second floor. There are twenty desks and a big white board. That is my desk, next to the window. My bag is under the desk. In my bag there is a notebook, a pencil, a pen and an eraser. Our teacher is at the door. "Open your books, please!" "Listen and repeat!" "Don't forget your homework!" Our classroom is bright and quiet.
q: Where is the writer's bag? (Yazarın çantası nerede?)
What is in the bag? (Çantada ne var?)
What is the classroom like? (Sınıf nasıl?)

A1.title: Ayşe's Day
A1.text: Ayşe always gets up at seven o'clock. She has breakfast with her brother and goes to school at half past seven. She comes home at four. First she does her homework, then she watches TV for an hour. She sometimes reads a book in the evening. She never goes to bed after ten o'clock on school days.
q: What does Ayşe do first after school? (Ayşe okuldan sonra ilk ne yapar?)
When does she go to school? (Ayşe okula ne zaman gider?)

A1.title: Our New Flat
A1.text: We have got a new flat in Bursa. There are three bedrooms, a kitchen, a bathroom and a living room. The living room is my favourite room. There is a big sofa next to the window and a small table in front of it. My cat sleeps under the table every afternoon. There isn't a garden, but there is a nice balcony.
q: Where does the cat sleep? (Kedi nerede uyur?)
Which sentence is true? (Hangi cümle doğru?)
The sofa is next to the window.
The kitchen is the favourite room.

A1.title: At the Market
A1.text: On Saturdays my mother and I go to the market. We buy bread, cheese, eggs and tomatoes. Apples are cheap today, so we buy two kilos. I want some orange juice, but it is expensive. "How much is a bottle of water?" my mother asks. "Five lira," says the man. We go home with three full bags.
q: Why do they buy two kilos of apples? (Neden iki kilo elma alıyorlar?)
What does the writer NOT buy? (Yazar neyi ALMIYOR?)

A1.title: Where Is the Museum?
A1.text: A tourist stops me on the street. "Excuse me, where is the museum?" she asks. I say, "Go straight and turn left at the bank. The museum is opposite the hospital." She can't speak Turkish, but she can speak a little English. She says thank you and smiles. Ten minutes later I see her in front of the museum.
q: Which language can the tourist speak? (Turist hangi dili konuşabiliyor?)

A1.title: A Rainy Day
A1.text: It is Saturday and it is raining in Trabzon. It is cold too. I am wearing my warm coat and my new shoes. My sister is wearing a yellow jacket. We are waiting for the bus and we are talking about the weather. "I hate rainy days," she says. "I don't," I answer. "Look, the sun is coming out!"
q: What is the weather like at first? (Başta hava nasıl?)
What is the sister wearing? (Kız kardeş ne giyiyor?)

A1.title: My Free Time
A1.text: I have a lot of free time at the weekend. I love swimming, so I go to the pool every Saturday morning. My brother enjoys cooking and he makes pancakes for us. My best friend likes playing games online, but I don't like it very much. On Sunday evenings we all enjoy reading together in the living room.
q: What does the writer do on Saturday mornings? (Yazar cumartesi sabahları ne yapar?)

A2.title: A Weekend in Bursa
A2.text: Last weekend I visited my grandparents in Bursa. We travelled by bus and arrived on Friday evening. I was tired, but I was excited too. On Saturday we walked around the old town and stayed at a small café for hours. On Sunday it rained, so we played cards at home. I wasn't bored at all. It was a lovely weekend.
q: What did they do on Sunday?
They walked in the old town.
How did the writer feel about the weekend?

A2.title: The Lost Wallet
A2.text: Yesterday something strange happened. I went to the park after school and sat on a bench. Then I saw a black wallet under the bench. I took it and looked inside. There was some money and an ID card. After that I went to the police station and gave it to an officer. Finally, the owner called me and said thank you. She bought me an ice cream!
q: Where did the writer find the wallet?
What did the writer do with the wallet?

A2.title: Summer Plans
A2.text: This summer my family is going to travel abroad for the first time. We are going to visit Greece. My father is going to book the tickets next week, and my mother is going to plan the trip. We are going to stay near the beach for five days, and then we are going to go to the mountains. I am going to pack my bag tomorrow!
q: Who is going to book the tickets?
How long will they stay near the beach?

A2.title: Big City, Small Town
A2.text: I live in Istanbul, but my cousin lives in a small town near Antalya. Istanbul is bigger and more crowded than her town. It is also more modern and more expensive. Her town is smaller, quieter and much cheaper. The weather there is better in winter, too. Which is the best place to live? I think both are beautiful in different ways.

A2.title: At the Doctor's
A2.text: Last Tuesday I didn't feel well. I had a headache and a sore throat, so I went to the doctor. She checked my temperature and said, "You have a cold. You should rest for two days and drink a lot of water. You shouldn't go to school tomorrow." She gave me some medicine. Now I feel much better and healthy again.
q: What was wrong with the writer?

A2.title: A Delayed Flight
A2.text: Our flight to London was at ten o'clock, but there was a long delay. The departure board said, "New departure time: 1 pm." My little brother was hungry, so I said, "I'll buy some sandwiches." My mother checked our passports and our luggage again. We finally arrived in London at four in the afternoon. It was a long journey, but we were happy.
q: What was the new departure time?
Why did the writer buy sandwiches?
The food on the plane was bad.

A2.title: Have You Ever...?
A2.text: My grandfather has had an exciting life. He has been to more than twenty countries. He has flown in a small plane over the Alps and he has eaten food from all over the world. He has met famous people, too. But he has never seen snow in the desert. "That is my next experience," he says, and laughs.
q: How many countries has the grandfather been to?

A2.title: School Rules
A2.text: At my new school there are some important rules. We must wear a uniform and we must be on time for every lesson. We mustn't use our phones in class, and we have to be quiet in the library. We don't have to bring lunch, because there is a school canteen. Students are allowed to play football in the garden at lunchtime.
q: Why don't students have to bring lunch?

B1.title: A Late Start
B1.text: Selin has worked as a nurse since 2019, but she has always wanted to be a pilot. Last year she finally decided to try. She has already finished her first flight lessons, although she hasn't taken the final exam yet. "I've just started, really," she says, "but I've improved a lot recently." Her friends think it is a brave career change, and she agrees that it is the biggest decision of her lifetime.
q: How long has Selin been a nurse?
She has passed the final exam.
She has finished her first lessons.

B1.title: The Old Neighbourhood
B1.text: When I was a child, we used to live in a narrow street in Izmir. Every evening the neighbours used to sit outside and chat while the children played. One night, while we were playing hide and seek, the electricity suddenly went off. Nobody was frightened; instead, someone started to sing. I still remember that evening as one of my happiest childhood memories.
q: What happened while the children were playing?

B1.title: After Graduation
B1.text: Burak will graduate next June. He hasn't decided what to do yet, but he will probably apply for a master's programme abroad. "If I get a scholarship, I'll go to Canada," he says. "Unless I find a good opportunity there, I'll stay in Turkey and look for a job." He has an appointment with a career advisor next week, and he will definitely ask her for advice as soon as he gets there.
q: What will Burak do if he gets a scholarship?
Why has he made an appointment?

B1.title: If I Won the Lottery
B1.text: My friends and I sometimes imagine what we would do if we were rich. Deniz says she would buy a small island and build a library there. Can wishes he could afford a house by the sea for his parents. I am not sure. If I won the lottery, I think I would travel for a year and then give most of the money to a children's hospital. "If I were you, I'd keep some for myself!" says Deniz.
q: What would Deniz build on her island?
A house by the sea for his parents

B1.title: Ancient City Discovered
B1.text: An ancient city has been discovered near the Black Sea coast. The ruins were found by local farmers last spring, and the site was visited by a team of archaeologists in July. According to the report, the city was probably built more than 2,500 years ago. Some buildings were damaged by an earthquake, but many objects have been preserved. The full results will be published next year.

B1.title: A Message from Ms Kaya
B1.text: Yesterday our English teacher told us that the exam had been moved to Friday. She explained that the classroom was needed for a meeting on Wednesday. Ali asked whether the exam would be longer, and she replied that it wouldn't. Some students complained that Friday was too late, but she promised to return our papers before the weekend. She also suggested that we revise units five and six.
q: The classroom was needed for a meeting.
To return the papers before the weekend

B1.title: The Woman Who Fixes Everything
B1.text: Every street has someone who helps everybody, and on ours it is Mrs Demir, whose small shop is next to the bakery. She is the neighbour who repairs broken radios, the friend who lends money without asking questions and the person whose advice everyone trusts. The shop where she works is tiny, but it is always full of people. She is generous, reliable and funny, a personality that is hard to describe in a few words.
q: Which word does NOT describe her in the text?

B1.title: Applying for the Job
B1.text: Dear Ms Aksoy, I am writing to apply for the position of junior designer, which was advertised on your website. I have attached my CV, which shows two years of experience in a busy agency. I enjoy working with colleagues and I am used to meeting deadlines. I would be happy to discuss the salary and the role in an interview. I look forward to hearing from you. Yours sincerely, Melis Aydın
q: Which job is Melis applying for?
What has Melis attached to the email?

B2.title: The Train I Missed
B2.text: Ten years ago I missed a train that would have changed my life. I had been offered an interview at a company in Berlin, but I overslept and arrived at the station two minutes late. If I had caught that train, I would probably be living in Germany now. At the time I blamed myself for weeks. In hindsight, however, missing it taught me a valuable lesson: had I not stayed, I would never have met my wife, who started working at my office a month later.
q: Why did the writer miss the train?
How does the writer see the event now?
What would have happened if he had caught the train?
He would have met his wife.
He would probably live in Germany.
He would have lost his job.
He would have stayed in Turkey.

B2.title: The Empty Office
B2.text: When the security guard arrived on Monday morning, the office was empty but the lights were on. A cup of coffee on the desk was still warm, so someone must have been there only minutes earlier. The window couldn't have been opened from outside, because it had been locked. There were muddy footprints near the door. The police assumed it might have been an employee, but the only witness, a cleaner, insisted that nobody had entered. The mystery remained unsolved for weeks.
q: Why did the guard think someone had just been there?

B2.title: Machines That Learn
B2.text: Artificial intelligence is being used in more areas than ever before. In hospitals, scans are now analysed by programs that have been trained on millions of images, and some studies suggest that their results are as reliable as those of experienced doctors. However, researchers warn that the data these systems are given can contain hidden biases. Many hospitals therefore have every decision checked by a human specialist. The aim, they argue, is not to replace doctors but to give them more time for patients.
q: The data can contain hidden biases.
According to the text, what is the aim of AI in hospitals?
To give doctors more time for patients
To reduce the number of hospitals

B2.title: A Greener Future
B2.text: By 2040, experts predict, most new cars sold in Europe will be electric, and many cities will have reduced their emissions by half. Renewable energy is already cheaper than coal in several countries. Yet the challenge remains enormous. Droughts are becoming more frequent, and thousands of species are at risk. Recycling helps, but scientists stress that reducing waste in the first place matters more. A sustainable future, they say, depends on decisions we will be making in the next ten years.
q: What do scientists say matters more than recycling?
Reducing waste in the first place
Renewable energy is always more expensive.
Renewable energy is cheaper than coal in some countries.
Emissions have already fallen by half.

B2.title: Should Homework Be Banned?
B2.text: Some educators argue that homework should be banned in primary schools. Although it is meant to strengthen learning, research suggests that young children gain little from it. Moreover, long assignments can cause stress and leave less time for play, which is essential for development. Supporters, however, point out that homework teaches responsibility and helps parents follow their children's progress. Despite the disagreement, most experts agree on one point: whereas short, meaningful tasks can help, hours of repetitive work rarely do.
q: What do supporters say homework teaches?
What do most experts agree on?

B2.title: A Bridge for the Neighbourhood
B2.text: For years, residents of the eastern district had to take two buses to reach the city centre. Last year the council finally agreed to build a footbridge across the river. Local volunteers organised meetings to make sure that the design met everyone's needs, including elderly people and wheelchair users. "I would rather walk ten minutes than wait an hour for a crowded bus," said one resident. Many now say it is time the city invested in affordable housing in the same way.
q: Who helped make sure the design met everyone's needs?
What do many residents now want?

B2.title: Sleep and Memory
B2.text: A growing body of research indicates that sleep plays a crucial role in learning. In one study, approximately 200 students were asked to memorise a list of words. Those who slept for eight hours performed significantly better the following day than those who stayed awake. Furthermore, the benefit was greatest for difficult material. Nevertheless, the researchers caution that the sample consisted only of university students; consequently, the findings may not apply to other age groups. Further studies are needed to assess these effects more widely.
q: Sleep has no effect on memory.
The sample included only university students.
In this text, 'crucial' is closest in meaning to ...

B2.title: Binge-Watching Culture
B2.text: Streaming platforms have changed the way we watch television. Instead of waiting a week for the next episode, many viewers now binge-watch a whole series in one weekend. Critics have come up with the idea that this habit makes stories less memorable, while fans argue that it is a piece of cake to stop whenever you like. Some people have given up their weekend plans for a new show, and others find out about the ending on social media before they finish. Either way, the old ritual of waiting together for the next episode now happens only once in a blue moon.
q: What does 'once in a blue moon' mean in the text?
